_provenance: S7a Task R3 -- tests/test_render_raster.cpp's RasterGolden.* tests. sha256 of the rendered BGRX8 pixel buffer (target.pixels, width*height*4 bytes, 160x120) for each fixed (scene, camera, options) triple built by that test file's own golden_scene_*()/camera fixtures. Depends on render/tessellate.hpp's tessellate_primitive() output for box/sphere/cylinder geometry -- tessellation_limits_version pins WHICH kTessellationDefaults these hashes were captured against, the same convention tests/golden/render/tessellation/manifest.json uses for its own corpus.
_changelog: Initial goldens, Task R3 (deterministic CPU rasterizer, first solid-shading + wireframe + overlay pass). REGENERATED at Task R6 (S7a): materials/lighting/sky/analytic-ground landed -- see _regeneration_note below for why all three hashes legitimately moved.
_regeneration_note: R6 (directional/ambient/sky lighting) and R7 (sun shadows) are EXPECTED to change every one of these hashes -- flat per-submesh material colour (this task's own shading model) will no longer be what a shaded-mode pixel shows once lighting lands. A hash changing alongside a matching commit that touches lighting/shadow code is an intentional, reviewed move; a hash changing with no such commit is rot. R6 REGENERATION (this change): every hash moved, and legitimately -- render()'s old flat clear colour is GONE, replaced by a vertical sky gradient (RenderScene::Lighting.sky_zenith/sky_horizon) plus an analytic ground for a scene with a standalone ground plane (none of these three fixtures has one, so their background is pure sky-gradient, not flat); DrawMode::shaded now Gouraud-shades every triangle from its per-vertex world-space normal via Lambert N.L + ambient (ruling SR-18) instead of a flat per-submesh colour, so box_shaded_with_overlays and cylinder_static_dynamic_box_top_down move for that reason too. sphere_wireframe_no_overlays uses DrawMode::wireframe, which stays deliberately UNLIT (raster_cpu.hpp's own header comment) -- its hash still moved, but ONLY because of the background sky gradient, not because its geometry's colour changed. R7 will legitimately move all three again (sun shadows); that is known and is not instability.
